extracted.intended_audience: applicants seeking admission to the USPTO registration (patent bar) examination (prospective patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed instructions and requirements for applying to sit for the USPTO registration (patent bar) examination, covering required documents, fees, application completion and updates, accommodations, exam format, test administration, and appeals/petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be complete for proper review by OED; applicants should carefully review information and documentation before submitting; incomplete applications are strongly discouraged and may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facsimile transmissions will not be accepted. See 37 CFR §§ 1.4(e) and 1.6(d)(1). An incomplete application, if not timely completed, will result in denial of admission and require filing a new application and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents for admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit specified documents to apply for admission to the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: (1) completed Application for Registration to Practice before the USPTO (Form PTO-158); (2) applicable application and registration examination fees; (3) official transcripts; (4) course descriptions (Category B only); (5) all other required documentation (e.g., evidence of qualifications, permanent residence, documents responsive to questions 14–21); (6) for aliens, copies of all documents submitted to and received from US immigration authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form completion and signature standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Application form must be completed in permanent ink or by computer and personally signed in accordance with 37 CFR § 1.4(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the entire application and General Requirements Bulletin before completing. Keep a copy of completed application papers. Do not use pencil. Signatures must be original; facsimile transmissions are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to update application
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided is continuing; applicants must report changes in writing until registered to practice before the USPTO in patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All changes, including changes of address, must be signed and dated; cannot be accepted by telephone, facsimile transmission, or e-mail. OED should be notified within 30 days of occurrence. Retain copies of all updates submitted to USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide complete legal name including first name, middle name (not initial), and last name on line 1a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence will use the applicant's complete name; failing to provide complete legal name may render the application incomplete. Check reasonable accommodations box at end of line 1a only if request and supporting documentation are attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name on ID must match application
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name on line 1b exactly as it appears on a valid, current government-issued photo identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same valid government ID must be presented for admission to the exam. Admission will be denied if the ID is invalid (e.g., expired) or if there is any difference between the name on the ID and the name on line 1b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact address and business contact rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the address where OED can communicate with applicant during the day between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. Eastern time; if OED is to communicate at a business, provide the business name and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government employees must enter department/agency name, mailing address and business telephone; may not use home or another business address. If notices are to be sent to home, supply home address on separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship, birth, and immigration information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide citizenship, date of birth, place of birth, visa classification, permanent resident status and registration number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line 2: country of citizenship. Line 3: date of birth. Line 4: city, state and country of birth. Line 5: visa classification if alien. Line 6: indicate permanent resident status and submit copy of both sides of permanent resident card if applicable. Line 7: provide alien registration number if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee selection and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must select and submit the appropriate application fee box and determine whether higher fees under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(10) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit the appropriate application fee may cause disapproval. Applicants subject to 11.7(h)/(k) must submit the §1.21(a)(10) fee for each determination regarding good moral character and reputation. Refund rules: $1,688.00 may be refundable under some circumstances; $118.00 application fee is non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration examination fee and commercial test administration fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration examination fee to USPTO must be submitted and a separate Prometric test administration fee will be charged by the commercial test administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application and registration exam fees may be paid with one check or credit card authorization. Prometric charges a separate administration fee. See lines 8a and 8b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for former USPTO employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Former patent examiners or other USPTO employees seeking a waiver of the examination must indicate so on line 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is under provisions of 37 CFR § 11.7(d). Check the appropriate box on line 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior applications/examinations/registrations disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose prior examination passage, prior applications for admission, prior registrations, and bar membership where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line 10: check if passed prior examination and give date. Line 11: indicate if previously applied for admission and give date. Line 12: provide prior registration number if previously registered to practice in patent cases. Line 13: check if member in good standing of U.S. court and list courts and bar numbers; do not submit certificate of good standing with application (original needed upon passing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral character and reputation disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer questions 14 through 21 with complete honesty and candor; any doubt should be resolved in favor of disclosure, and there is a continuing duty to update these responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements may lead to denial, revocation, or discipline. Provide detailed statement with all relevant facts and dates even when answering 'no.' A complete disclosure should include (a) full written explanation (where applicant was, what doing), (b) identification of law enforcement authority, (c) statement of charges and disposition, (d) sanctions and compliance, (e)-(f) copies of documents/records and court files or documentation of requests for such records, (g) for federal debt, records showing satisfaction or payment arrangement, (h) records showing sanctions and compliance. If unable to obtain records, include documentation of requests and responses. Failure to include information treated as incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of registration selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether applying for registration for All Patent Matters or Design Patent Matters Only on line 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the appropriate box on line 22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: List all degrees and attach official transcripts for each degree and official course descriptions if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transcripts and course descriptions (especially Category B applicants) with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted payment methods to USPTO and related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Government fees must be paid in U.S. dollars and in acceptable forms at time of application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable forms: cashier's or certified check, Treasury note, or USPS money order. Other forms (including personal checks, credit cards or electronic funds transfer) may delay or cancel credit until collection. Checks/money orders payable to Director of the USPTO. Cash not accepted. Credit card payments require specifying amount and card info; Office not liable if card info on non-standard forms becomes public. Credit card form link provided. $54 service charge for each payment refused or charged back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpayment consequences and returned-check policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonpayment (including returned checks or charged-back credit cards) can result in refusal of admission, withdrawal of admission, denial of registration even if applicant passed, and requirement to pay prior outstanding fees before future admissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED will notify applicant of nonpayment and deadline to complete fees. If admitted but payment later refused/discovered, registration denied until fees and processing fee paid. Example: returned check may require applicant to pay prior $118 + $54 processing fee or additional amounts depending on circumstances. Do not close accounts before payment clears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no filing deadline for submitting an application for the commercially administered computerized examination; applications processed year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incomplete application, if not timely completed, will result in denial and require reapplication with fees. Fees from one application are not deferred to another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application specifics for Category B and aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: Category B applicants must submit course descriptions and any other documentation; aliens must submit all required information and documentation with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to gather all required information before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application notice and 60-day cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: If application is incomplete, OED will notify applicant and provide a 60-day time frame to complete the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply must be signed per 37 CFR § 1.4(e). Failure to respond within 60 days, or continued insufficiency after submission of additional materials, will result in disapproval. Disapproved applicants will receive a detailed explanation. $226 exam fee refunded to disapproved applicant; $118 application fee is not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing instructions and confirmation of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide correct mailing address and keep copies of every document; include a self-addressed, postage-paid postcard to request acknowledgment of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address: Mail Stop OED, Director of the USPTO, PO Box 1450, Alexandria, VA. For hand delivery/courier, obtain street address by phone. OED will stamp postcard with receipt date and mail it back; postcard is not verification that all items were present. Do not call OED about status unless four weeks have passed after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process after application submission
rubrics_metrics.description: OED reviews applications for completeness and sufficiency of scientific and technical training; qualified applicants receive admission letter; incomplete applications receive notice of missing items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is incomplete if missing information on form, fees, transcripts, or other required documentation. Both application and $226 examination fee must be submitted to receive an evaluation of qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO identification number assignment and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are issued a USPTO Identification Number which must be used on all subsequent correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All notifications include USPTO ID number; this number is critical for identifying the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review by OED Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants dissatisfied with disapproval may petition the OED Director for review upon payment of the applicable fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must bear original signature and be submitted within 60 days of disapproval notice. Additional documentation may be submitted. Outcomes: admission granted, OED staff decision affirmed, or final decision sent. Registration examination fee will be refunded to applicant in due course if appropriate; $118 fee not refundable. Petitions after 60 days are dismissed as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review by USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Final decisions by the OED Director may be reviewed by petition to the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires payment of fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(5)(ii) and filing within 30 days of the OED Director's final decision. Late petitions are dismissed as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely filing methods and constructive receipt rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods are specified for timely filing replies or petitions: first class mail/hand delivery, certificate of mailing (37 CFR § 1.8), and Priority Mail Express® (37 CFR §1.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First class mail or hand-delivered papers are stamped received on the date of receipt. Certificate of mailing procedure can be used if all § 1.8 requirements are met (facsimile transmission not acceptable). For Priority Mail Express®, the 'date-in' on the mailing label is the effective date; ensure USPS employee records date-in on the label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations package required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants requesting reasonable accommodation must submit a Request for Reasonable Accommodation package (Form PTO-158RA) consisting of an Applicant's Statement and a Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check the reasonable accommodations box on Form PTO-158 if the request is included. After admission, separate notification of accommodations granted will be mailed. Scheduling with Prometric may take up to 30 days; contact Prometric Reasonable Accommodations Department to schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for completing RA package
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must provide detailed responses in the Applicant's Statement and submit a completed Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement and/or other acceptable medical evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may use additional paper if necessary. The completed package should be submitted with Form PTO-158 or separately to Mail Stop OED as instructed. Failure to provide requested information may result in insufficient information to grant accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RA reapplication and documentation currency
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who previously received accommodations must submit a new Applicant's Statement with each new application; provide a new Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement if the impairment is temporary or has changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency determines accommodations based on current impact of impairment on testing activity. For chronic or long-term conditions a new Licensed Health Care Professional's Statement may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination content sources and reference materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination questions are designed to test knowledge of applicable patent laws, rules, procedures, and ability to apply them; may include ethics/professional conduct questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be familiar with patent statutes and USPTO rules of practice (Parts 1, 3, 11, 41, 42 CFR), MPEP, and other USPTO policy/procedure references. Reference materials cited will be available during the examination. OED will announce updates via Official Gazette and Practitioners web page; applicable reference materials control in event of conflict with MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination format and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination consists of 100 multiple-choice questions administered in two sessions: 50 questions in a three-hour morning session and 50 in a three-hour afternoon session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each question has five choices. A total of six hours is permitted for completion of the examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited items at examination site
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not bring documents, materials, machines, or electronic devices into the examination area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited items include computers, telephones, recording devices, cameras, and typewriters. For commercially-administered exams reference materials will be available on the computer delivering the examination. Prometric provides storage lockers for items not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination preparation materials and OED non-counseling policy
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP and other reference materials are available on the USPTO website; OED will not counsel applicants on statutes/rules or recommend preparation courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot identify or recommend courses or offer advice on special training required to qualify to practice before the Office as a patent attorney or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination results and post-pass registration instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Official examination results will be released by OED and mailed to applicants; passing applicants will receive instructions for completing registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercially-administered examination takers receive unofficial results at the computer at the end of the examination day and official results by mail soon after.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test administration: admission letter and name consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission letter is sent to qualified applicants with instructions; applicants must verify personal information on the admission letter matches their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name on the admission letter should match the name given on line 1b of the application and will be provided to Prometric for entrance to the examination site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling window and extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission letter specifies a scheduling time period; after expiration applicant cannot schedule and must file a new application and fees. Extensions are available for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions cost $124.00 under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(b)(4)(ii) and may be requested and granted an unlimited number of times if received before the scheduling period expires. Fee must be included; if request received after expiration the fee will be refunded. Prometric may charge separate scheduling/rescheduling fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prometric fee collection and scheduling options
rubrics_metrics.description: Prometric collects the commercially-administered examination administration fee at time of scheduling; applicants schedule directly with Prometric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prometric collects no fees at testing centers. Scheduling options include Prometric.com, Prometric toll-free customer service, or contacting local testing center. Applicants are urged to schedule promptly due to site availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prometric cancel/late/no-show/reschedule policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Prometric enforces specific policies for late arrival, rescheduling, cancellation, and no-shows that may affect admission and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrive 30 minutes early. Late arrival results in denial of admission. Reschedule via Prometric website or the reserved toll-free number. If testing center cannot provide exam, it will be rescheduled to first available appointment at no charge. Failure to appear for scheduled exam may result in loss of eligibility at Prometric and forfeiture of USPTO fees; applicant may contact OED to reset eligibility if sufficient time remains in testing period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required at testing center
rubrics_metrics.description: For admission to commercially-administered examination, applicants must bring a current, valid State or Federal government-issued photo ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: driver's license or passport. The ID must match the name on the admission letter (line 1b).
